A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GraphPFN and contain readable main text, appendices A–E, tables, equations and figures. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original benchmark results in Tables 1–2, alongside graph-prior analyses, component ablations, ECOC evaluations and runtime measurements in the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations without random input features in Appendix C, Table 7.

M1.justification: The LimiX backbone, graph adapters, synthetic prior, training objectives and default random-feature augmentation remain unchanged. V4 tests feature removal as an ablation of the existing method.

E1.justification: The synthetic training distribution and evaluated datasets and tasks are unchanged, including the appendix ECOC datasets. The new ablation uses the same eight GraphLand datasets.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds GraphPFN without random features as a comparison variant in ICL and finetuning, each with and without ensembling. All previously evaluated comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: V4 introduces controlled evaluations omitting the eight random input features across the existing ICL/finetuning and ensemble/light settings. Previously reported splits, metrics and default experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds one focused ablation testing the contribution of random input features, with four configurations evaluated across eight datasets. Existing prior, MGM, adapter and ensembling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 10 experimental runs, or five for non-PFN GFMs, and report means and standard deviations. The added ablation follows the existing reporting practice; no new uncertainty procedure or increased run count is stated.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds 32 per-dataset results. For example, the new ensemble ICL evaluation without random features scores 66.95±0.14 on twitch-views, versus the retained 73.20±0.08 with those features. Average ranks change with the enlarged comparison set; all retained per-dataset means and standard deviations remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of graph generation, SCM attribute generation and graph statistics are unchanged. No formal assumption, theorem, proof or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and principal conclusions retain the same scientific claims, including best finetuning results on 11 of 13 main datasets. Local wording edits do not change their scope.

C2.justification: The substantive limitations and interpretations of pretraining, adapters and graph priors are retained. The new random-feature paragraph reports an empirical outcome without adding a mechanism explanation or applicability qualification.

D1.justification: The eight random features and their use in each forward pass were already disclosed in v3, Section 5.1. Implementation, hardware, preprocessing, ensembling and code-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The references, related-work discussion and positioning relative to concurrent NodePFN work are unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized wording edits to Observation 2, the conclusion and the limitations introduction, and adds a short random-feature paragraph. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 7 expands from 15 to 19 rows and defines the new abbreviation in its caption. Several appendix tables are reduced in size, with local text reflow. All figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new ablation isolates an augmentation whose contribution v3 did not directly test, documenting its particularly large ICL effect on twitch-views and smaller or mixed effects elsewhere. This modestly strengthens empirical support for the existing design. The more compact appendix tables impose only a small readability cost.
